messages:
jamal (support): Hey team, ACME reported repeated 429s and tail latency spikes on their Dedicated pool this morning. They say it started after they increased context length to 65k tokens. Can someone triage?

maria (sre): Noted. Any request IDs or sample logs from the customer? 65k context is large — could be KV cache pressure.

jamal (support): Paste from customer: 
```
2026-02-14T08:12:03Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 serve: throttled: kv_cache_full evict_rate=0.98 mem_frag=0.72 active_kv_entries=12.3M
2026-02-14T08:12:04Z WARN request_id=efgh5678 latency=1200ms queue_wait=980ms
```

jamal (support): They also noted that autoscale didn't spin more GPUs, pool is Dedicated-small (4xA10G).

alex (eng-runtime): That log lines up with aggressive KV cache eviction + fragmentation. At high context lengths we keep more KV pages which increases per-worker memory. Fragmentation ratio 0.72 is high.

maria (sre): Did the pool hit host-level OOM or kernel slab pressure? Any dmesg or OOM killer evidence?

jamal (support): Customer sent dmesg snippet, no OOM kill, just cgroup oom_score_adj events and some Xfer failures.

alex (eng-runtime): Likely noisy neighbor + long-context workload causing per-process KV footprints to grow beyond what the dedicated allocation expected. Eviction is racing with new requests => throttling to keep QoS. Autoscaler might not have triggered because CPU/GPU utilization stayed under thresholds (we measure util, not KV pressure).

maria (sre): Repro steps we should try before paging infra: 1) Recreate workload in staging with same context distribution (few requests with 50-70k tokens). 2) Toggle model kv_cache_size and eviction policy to LRU aggressive. 3) Monitor mem_frag and active_kv_entries.

alex (eng-runtime): For a faster mitigation we can: 1) Temporarily increase kv_cache_capacity on the pool (per-customer override) to reduce eviction churn. 2) Lower per-request max_context for that customer to 50k while we investigate. 3) Add a KV-pressure metric to autoscaler (tracked).

tara (account): ACME is blocked in prod. They asked for ETA. They prefer config changes rather than shifting workload.

maria (sre): I'll schedule a quick maintenance window to bump kv_cache_capacity for their Dedicated-small pool and enable an eviction backoff to avoid tight loop evictions. That should reduce 429s.

alex (eng-runtime): Also will open a patch to make autoscaler consider kv_pressure (mem_frag + eviction_rate) as a signal. Short-term code change: if eviction_rate > 0.8 and mem_frag > 0.6, scale up a node.

jamal (support): I told customer we'll try config change now and follow up with root cause and a timeline. They asked for exact commands so they can repro.

alex (eng-runtime): Repro command snippet for staging (internal):
```
# run loadgen with long-context profile
./loadgen --model rwd-large --concurrency 8 --context-dist long-65k --duration 15m --trace output.json
# collect kv stats from node
curl http://node-metrics.local:9100/kv_stats | jq '. | {eviction_rate, mem_frag, active_kv_entries}'
```

maria (sre): After we bump config I'll monitor for 30m. If 429s stop and eviction_rate drops <0.2 we'll keep change and plan infra/autoscaler fix. If not, escalate to infra for host memory tuning.

sre-bot: Incident created -> INC-2026-0214-kv-pressure, severity=P2, assigned=maria

jamal (support): Thanks. ACME appreciates the quick response. Will update thread with customer confirmation after the maintenance. :thumbsup:
